title: AIP-C01 Skill 1.6.3: Govern Prompts with Versions, Approval and Audit
html:
AIP-C01 Skill 1.6.3: Govern Prompts with Versions, Approval and Audit

A hands-on lab with prompt versions, an approval step, an S3 template repository, CloudTrail and CloudWatch Logs. Task 1.6, post 3 of 7.

[IMAGE: cover-1-6-3.png — alt: "Skill 1.6.3: Governing prompts"]

AIP-C01 Hands-on Labs · Domain 1 · Task 1.6: Implement prompt engineering strategies and governance for FM interactions · Post 3 of 7. Hands-on lab, about 30 minutes.

A prompt is code that changes behaviour in production. Someone edits the returns assistant's prompt on a Friday afternoon, the assistant starts promising refunds it shouldn't, and on Monday nobody can say who changed what, or roll it back quickly. Skill 1.6.1 put the prompt in one managed place. This skill puts a process around it: changes are reviewed, published as versions, and traceable.

What AWS says

Skill 1.6.3: Implement comprehensive prompt management and governance systems to ensure consistency and oversight of FM operations (for example, by using Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management to create parameterized templates and approval workflows, Amazon S3 to store template repositories, AWS CloudTrail to track usage, Amazon CloudWatch Logs to log access).

What it means in plain words

  • Parameterized templates: prompts with variables ({{policy}}, {{question}}) so one reviewed template serves every request.
  • Approval workflows: nobody publishes their own change; someone else signs off first.
  • S3 template repository: a versioned bucket (or Git) holding the source of each template, with its owner and change note.
  • CloudTrail to track usage: a record of who created, updated or published prompts, and when.
  • CloudWatch Logs to log access: model invocation logging, recording what each call sent and received.

[IMAGE: t1-6-3-lifecycle.png — alt: "The prompt lifecycle: author, review, promote, release, audit changes, audit use, with the evidence each stage leaves"]

What we're going to do

  1. Submit version 2 of the returns assistant template to a versioned S3 repository, tagged pending-review.
  2. Try to promote it to Prompt Management: refused.
  3. Approve it as a reviewer, then promote it: the managed prompt is updated and an immutable version 2 is created.
  4. List the versions and see exactly which lines changed.
  5. Find the changes in CloudTrail, and (optionally) the invocations in CloudWatch Logs.

What you'll learn

  • How draft, versions and version ARNs work in Prompt Management.
  • How to gate publishing behind an approval.
  • The difference between auditing changes (CloudTrail) and auditing use (invocation logs).
  • How rollback works when applications pin a version.

What you'll need

  • Time and cost: about 30 minutes, under US$0.01
  • Region: us-west-2
  • Access: Python 3.10+ with boto3; an S3 bucket in us-west-2; the returns-assistant prompt from the Skill 1.6.1 lab (its ID is the part of PROMPT_ARN after prompt/ and before :); permission to read CloudTrail events
  • Files: github.com/prasanth2006z/aip-c01-labs, folder domain-1/task-1.6/skill-1.6.3-governance

The lab

Step 1: Submit a template change

pip install boto3
export LAB_BUCKET=your-bucket-name PROMPT_ID=XXXXXXXXXX
python governance_lab.py submit

templates/returns-assistant.json is the source of version 2. Besides the system prompt, it records who owns it and why it changed:

"version_note": "v2: adds the warranty rule and asks for the customer's order number",
"owner": "support-ai-team",
"variables": ["policy", "question"],

The script turns on bucket versioning, uploads the file to prompt-templates/returns-assistant.json and tags it status=pending-review. Every upload is now a recoverable S3 object version.

Step 2: Try to promote it

python governance_lab.py promote
Refused: template status is 'pending-review'. A reviewer must approve it first.

The promote step is the only path into Prompt Management, and it checks approval first.

Step 3: Approve, then promote

python governance_lab.py approve
python governance_lab.py promote

Approval adds status=approved, approved-by and approved-at tags. Promote then calls UpdatePrompt (which changes the prompt's draft) and CreatePromptVersion, which snapshots the draft as version 2. The version's description records the change note, the approver and the S3 object version it came from, so every published version traces back to its reviewed source.

Version 1, which applications were using, is untouched. Versions are immutable.

Step 4: Compare versions

python governance_lab.py versions

You'll see DRAFT, 1 and 2 with their descriptions, then the lines version 2 added:

  + - If the item is faulty rather than unwanted, mention the 2-year power tool warranty.
  + - Ask for the order number if the customer hasn't given one.

Applications call a version ARN such as ...:prompt/XXXXXXXXXX:2. Releasing is a config change to that ARN; rolling back is changing it back to :1. No one edits a live prompt.

Step 5: Audit changes with CloudTrail

python governance_lab.py audit

The script looks up CreatePrompt, UpdatePrompt, CreatePromptVersion and DeletePrompt events from the last 24 hours, with who made each call. CloudTrail answers “who changed the prompt, and when?”. New events can take up to 15 minutes to appear.

Step 6 (optional): Audit use with invocation logs

In the Bedrock console, open Settings → Model invocation logging, enable it with destination CloudWatch Logs and log group /aws/bedrock/invocations. Run the Skill 1.6.1 ask step again, then:

export INVOCATION_LOG_GROUP=/aws/bedrock/invocations
python governance_lab.py logs

Each record shows the model, the caller's identity and (in the full log) the complete request and response. That answers “what exactly did the model receive?”, which CloudTrail can't: CloudTrail records API calls, not prompt content. Because these logs contain full prompts and responses, restrict access to the log group and set a retention period.

In production

  • Authors can write to the template repository; only a CI/CD role can call UpdatePrompt and CreatePromptVersion.
  • Approval is a different identity: a pull request review, a CodePipeline manual approval action, or a Step Functions task that waits for a reviewer.
  • The pipeline runs the prompt test suite (Skill 1.6.4) before it creates a version.
  • Applications pin a version ARN, often read from AWS AppConfig (Skill 1.2.2), so rollout and rollback need no deployment.

Common pitfalls

  • Applications call the draft: the draft changes whenever someone edits it. Always call a numbered version.
  • UpdatePrompt fails: it replaces the whole prompt definition, so send the name and every variant, not just the changed text.
  • Looking for prompt text in CloudTrail: it isn't there. Enable model invocation logging.
  • No CloudTrail events yet: wait up to 15 minutes, and check you're in us-west-2.

Clean up

  • Delete prompt-templates/ from your bucket, including all object versions.
  • If you enabled it, turn off model invocation logging and delete the log group.
  • Delete the returns-assistant prompt when you've finished Task 1.6.

What to remember

  • Prompt Management: a draft you edit, immutable numbered versions you publish, version ARNs applications pin.
  • Template source in a versioned S3 bucket or Git, with owner and change note.
  • Approval by someone else before a version is created; only a pipeline role publishes.
  • Rollback = point the application at the previous version ARN.
  • Who changed prompts → CloudTrail. What the model received → model invocation logging to CloudWatch Logs or S3.

The exam scenarios for this skill are in post 7 of this task: Task 1.6 Exam Notes.
